already_extracted_claims: The source describes doing full G4 analysis, heat map analysis, survey analysis, session recordings, and creating roadmaps and frameworks.
The source recommends learning from wins, taking more time to see why tests lose, and implementing changes in winning and future tests.

The source says cross-functional teamwork involves working with designers, developers, copywriters, and CRO strategists, and that this happens when there is a high volume of people coming through the tests.
The source says quantitative data is the what and qualitative data is the why.

The source recommends funnel and drop-off analysis; under 300,000 sessions full GA or tracking software analysis is not required, but you should look at where people drop off and why. If straight from ad to PDP, analyze PDP, cart, checkout, thank you page, and upsell if using OCU or Zipify.
The source says everyone, whether doing 10,000 or 10 million sessions per month, needs to install a heat map on the product page and do heat map analysis of clicks, scrolls, and scroll depth.

The source says false clicks or rage clicks occur when people click where they think a button or link is but it is not, and that eliminating false clicks has produced massive uplifts and wins in high-volume stores.
The source says the way to scale on paid media effectively is by finding your offer: what sells through cold media and what sells profitably through buying media online.

The source recommends user testing and usability studies, including getting people onto the site, surveying them, doing proper user testing and user interviews, and calling customers to ask why they purchased, whether the experience was good, and what was unclear.
The source says to set up post-purchase surveys, using No Commerce or Komerse, and ask at least two questions: what made you purchase today and what made you almost not purchase today.

The source says answers to the second post-purchase survey question, such as not knowing how long results take, can be used to change front-end copy or angle, for example saying see noticeable results in the first six weeks.

If there is no post-purchase survey but there is a list to survey, the source recommends setting up a one-time survey with a tool like Typeform, emailing VIPs and customers with important feedback questions, and offering a chance to win a $250 Amazon gift card.

If there are over 500 to 1,000 reviews, the source recommends exporting reviews to CSV, uploading them to a GPT or AI, and prompting it to find commonalities, tone of voice, buzzwords, key phrases, friction points, and objections to answer on the front end.

The source recommends buying from your own store within the past month, testing the experience on mobile, desktop, and tablet, handing a mobile phone to a 70-year-old grandma to watch her buy, spotting annoying bugs, and doing full UX/UI audits to ensure a nice buying experience.

The source says combining qualitative and quantitative data reveals what is happening and why, and this combined data is needed to set up effective conversion rate optimization through landing pages, offer price testing, or comprehensive AB testing at velocity if a bigger store. It says to do these two things in full.

The source says that over 300,000 sessions, all qualitative and quantitative analysis should be done as non-negotiable and will make drastically more money; under that, the bolded items are the ones to focus on.
The source asserts that data is singlehandedly the most important thing in the conversion rate optimization arsenal.
The source warns that many brands hide important information below the fold.
The source lists price and offer testing as part of quantitative analysis must-dos.
The source reports annoying bugs where exit pops or cookie modals appear above the CTA on product pages.
The source says heatmap.com tracks based on revenue rather than just clicks.
The source says setting up post-purchase surveys is probably single-handedly the most effective way to optimize a store.
The source says customer surveys and feedback loops are essential.
The source says that under 300,000 sessions, you need an agency or must spend the time and resource to do the analysis yourself.
The source describes a full comprehensive audit for clients over 300,000 sessions, taking two to three weeks and producing about a 100-page findings document around audience wants and objections.
